obj.cause: The upper bound is inclusive, so n == len(s) is treated as valid. For s='ab', len is 2, so n=2 passes the check and s[2] raises IndexError. Valid indices are 0 .. len(s)-1.
obj.change: Make the upper bound exclusive: compare n with len(s) using < instead of <= so n == len(s) returns ''.
obj.verification: Re-run assert nth_char('ab', 2) == ''. Also check nth_char('ab', 0) == 'a', nth_char('ab', 1) == 'b', and out-of-range cases like n=-1 and n=3 return ''.
